prompt.context: Your client is a national burrito chain with 100 locations. There has been a widespread flu virus growing in the U.S. which has the potential to hurt their business. They need your help deciding how they should respond to the virus in NYC specifically, and what the implications will be for their brand.
prompt.question: How should Tres Burritos respond to the flu virus in NYC, and what will be the profitability implications of their chosen response?

clarifying_info.q: How many locations does Tres Burritos have in NYC?

clarifying_info.a: They sell 3 types of burritos, along with guacamole, salsa, and other sides.

clarifying_info.q: How do they currently serve customers?
clarifying_info.a: All sales come from grab-and-go takeout orders. Tres Burritos does not currently offer delivery.

clarifying_info.q: What is the client's primary goal?
clarifying_info.a: Their main goal is maintaining a net positive profit. They are also concerned about how their actions in NY will affect the national brand.

clarifying_info.q: How long is the virus expected to last?
clarifying_info.a: The virus is projected to last for 3 months.

clarifying_info.q: How is Tres Burritos responding in other cities?
clarifying_info.a: We do not know how Tres Burritos is responding in other cities.

exhibits.title: Income Statement – Monthly (per restaurant)
exhibits.shows: A monthly income statement for one Tres Burritos restaurant, showing revenue and expense line items.

exhibits.shows: A pie chart breaking down where NYC Tres Burritos customers reside.

framework: Profitability analysis: assess current revenue (product mix, number of orders, average check) and costs (fixed: rent, equipment, SG&A, marketing; variable: labor, COGS)
Options for responding to the virus: Stay Open, Close, or Modify (offer delivery/curbside pickup, partial closures, change hours, close only some stores)
External considerations: virus duration/spread/location, competitor actions, NYC population behavior, Tres Burritos response in other cities
Brand/reputational implications of each option at the national level

questions.prompt: What should Tres Burritos consider in responding to the virus?
questions.guidance: Candidate should structure thinking around: (1) Profitability — revenue impact and cost structure; (2) Response options beyond binary open/close — modify hours, offer delivery, partial closures, curbside; (3) External factors — virus trajectory, competitor behavior, customer behavior, national brand consistency. A strong candidate goes beyond open vs. close immediately.

questions.prompt: How would you evaluate the three main options — Stay Open, Close, or Modify Hours/Services — for responding to the virus?
questions.guidance: Candidate should build a structured comparison (e.g., pro/con matrix). Key points: Stay Open (pros: continue sales, serve community, customer loyalty; cons: bad reputation, safety risk, pay both fixed and variable costs). Close (pros: no variable costs, no virus spread risk; cons: still have fixed costs, no revenue, possible layoffs, bad reputation). Modify (pros: continue some sales, potential new revenue streams via delivery/apps; cons: fixed + some variable costs, safety risk, unknown customer response, customers may defect to competitors). Candidate should conclude that profitability data is needed to choose among options and ask for it.

questions.prompt: Governor Andy Hamilton has decided restaurants cannot stay open as usual — they can only offer delivery. What will the virus's impact be on Tres Burritos' profitability per location over the 3-month period?
questions.guidance: Candidate should request current financials (Exhibit 1) and the virus impact assumptions. They should recognize the one-time delivery setup cost affects only Month 1, and calculate EBITDA for each month separately before summing. Takeaway: although EBITDA is negative in Month 1, total 3-month EBITDA under delivery is positive ($37K), which is better than closing (where fixed costs still apply with zero revenue).

math.setup: Current monthly revenue = $100K; Current total expenses = $70K (COGS $10K + Wages $35K + SG&A $5K + Fixed Overhead $20K). New: Revenue drops 10%, COGS increases 10%, one-time delivery setup cost = $20K. Virus lasts 3 months.
math.answer: 3-month EBITDA per location = $37,000 (vs. $90,000 currently), a ~60% decline. Bonus: total across all 10 NYC locations = $370,000.

questions.prompt: What are some possible ways to improve EBITDA if Tres Burritos keeps restaurants open and offers delivery?
questions.guidance: Candidate should brainstorm both revenue-increase and cost-reduction levers. Strong candidates think creatively beyond the obvious (e.g., selling raw ingredients, 3rd-party delivery apps to cut setup cost).

brainstorming.prompt: What are possible ways to improve EBITDA if Tres Burritos keeps restaurants open and offers delivery?

categories.name: Increase Revenue
ideas: Offer groceries — sell raw ingredients directly to customers from their kitchen
Partner with other local restaurants to drive mutual traffic
Raise prices to partially offset volume decline
Increase presence on 3rd party delivery apps (Seamless, Caviar, etc.) to capture more orders

categories.name: Decrease Costs
ideas: Reduce staff / optimize scheduling to lower wage costs
Close some underperforming NYC locations to cut fixed overhead
Limit menu to fewer items to reduce COGS complexity
Reduce the $20K delivery setup cost by partnering with an existing delivery platform (Seamless, Caviar) instead of building own delivery infrastructure

recommendation: Recommend Tres Burritos offer delivery across its 10 NYC locations for the 3-month virus period
While EBITDA declines by ~60% (from $90K to $37K per location over 3 months, or $370K total for NYC), this is far preferable to closing, which would still incur fixed costs with zero revenue
The delivery option also protects the national brand by demonstrating community responsiveness
risks: Revenues decline more than the projected 10%, worsening the EBITDA impact
Customers shift to competitors during the virus and do not return afterward
Risk of spreading the disease through food handling or delivery personnel
Problems with the new delivery operation could damage the Tres Burritos national brand
next_steps: Identify and sign a delivery partner (e.g., Seamless, Caviar) and plan logistics to launch quickly
Explore further cost reductions (reduced staff, limited menu) to improve the $37K EBITDA outcome
Monitor what Tres Burritos and competitors are doing in other cities to align the national response strategy
